statement_record.book: A logical instance of the Yoneda technique: in the propositional calculus, to show φ and ψ interderivable it suffices to show that for EVERY formula θ, θ ⊢ φ iff θ ⊢ ψ — i.e. the poset case of Cor 8.5, objects with pointwise-equivalent representable down-sets are isomorphic.

In particular nothing in-tree records the step that makes the remark useful in a thin category — that a natural transformation between representables IS just a pointwise family of entailments (naturality being automatic when hom-setoids are trivial), so that 'for all θ, θ ⊢ φ ↔ θ ⊢ ψ' already yields yφ ≅ yψ and hence φ ≅ ψ.

evidence.intree_statement: #[export] Program Instance Yoneda_Embedding `(C : Category) : ∀ A B : C, Presheaves [Hom ─,A] [Hom ─,B] ≊ A ~> B.   (* ≊ is isomorphism of the two setoids in Sets: the setoid of natural transformations yA ⟹ yB and the hom-setoid A ~> B *)

Corollary Yoneda_Embedding' (C: Category) (c d : C) : @IsIsomorphism Sets {| carrier := hom d c |} {| carrier := hom (fobj[C] c) (fobj[C] d) |} {| morphism := @fmap _ _ (Curried_Hom C) c d; proper_morphism := fmap_respects _ _ |}.   (* fmap[y] is itself the bijection, so ϑ determines a unique h with y h = ϑ *)

statement_record.book: Methodological consequence of Thm 8.3: to construct an arrow h : A → B in a locally small C it suffices to construct a natural transformation ϑ : yA → yB in Sets^(C^op), since then there is a UNIQUE h with ϑ = y h. This is useful because the presheaf category has far more structure than C (complete, cocomplete, cartesian closed — established in 8.5–8.7), so presheaves extend C by 'ideal elements'.
statement_record.intree: Yoneda_Embedding : ∀ A B : C, Presheaves [Hom ─,A] [Hom ─,B] ≊ A ~> B — a setoid isomorphism (hence a bijection with the ≈-uniqueness the setoid setting affords) between natural transformations of representables and morphisms A ~> B; equivalently Yoneda_Embedding', which exhibits fmap[Curried_Hom C] itself as an isomorphism in Sets.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the remark's own assertion (existence AND uniqueness of the h inducing a given ϑ), stated as an iso of hom-setoids rather than a bijection of sets — the faithful setoid rephrasing. Two honest caveats: (i) uniqueness is up to the hom-setoid's ≈, which is the library's notion of equality of morphisms throughout; (ii) the remark's MOTIVATION — that presheaf categories are complete, cocomplete and cartesian closed — is forward-referenced to 8.5–8.7 and is largely NOT in-tree (see awodey:8.5:prop7, awodey:8.6:cor9 in this batch: no `Complete`/`Cocomplete` instance and no closed structure exists for any functor category); Instance/Fun.v:101-105 records that inheritance only as a header comment.

The remark's OPERATIVE assertion is exactly Thm 8.3 restated — for every ϑ : yA ⟹ yB there is a unique h with ϑ = y h — and that is Yoneda_Embedding, verified at Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:231-232 `#[export] Program Instance Yoneda_Embedding `(C : Category) : ∀ A B : C, Presheaves [Hom ─,A] [Hom ─,B] ≊ A ~> B` (with `Presheaves {U C} := [U^op, C]`, Theory/Sheaf.v:127, so the ambient category is the presheaf category as Awodey requires), and Yoneda_Embedding' at Functor/Hom.v:109. evidence.intree_statement: Definition Complete {C : Category} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Limit F.
Class Limit `(F : J ⟶ C) := { limit_cone : Cone F; ump_limits : ∀ N : Cone F, ∃! u : N ~> limit_cone, ∀ x : J, vertex_map[limit_cone] ∘ u ≈ @vertex_map _ _ _ _ (@coneFrom _ _ _ N) x }.
Lemma Cone_Natural_Transform `(F : [J, C]) : ∀ N : C, Δ[J](N) ⟹ F ↔ Cone[N] F.

statement_record.book: E is complete if for every small J and every F : J → E there is a limit L together with a cone η : ΔL → F in E^J which is universal among arrows ΔE → F out of constant functors; thus a cone with vertex E is exactly an arrow ΔE → F in E^J.
statement_record.intree: Complete {C} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Limit F, where Limit F is a cone with the universal property `∀ N : Cone F, ∃! u : N ~> limit_cone, ∀ x, φ_x ∘ u ≈ ψ_x`; and Cone_Natural_Transform proves Δ[J](N) ⟹ F ↔ Cone[N] F, so the cone presentation and Awodey's Δ presentation are interchangeable in-tree.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Two presentation differences, both bridged in-tree: (i) cones are primitive (apex + coherent leg family, Structure/Cone.v:24/51) rather than defined as arrows out of Δ, but Cone_Natural_Transform (and Cone_Comma / Instance/Cones/Comma.v's functorial `Cones F ≅[Cat] (Δ ↓ =(F))`) identify the two; (ii) smallness of J is not an explicit hypothesis — the definition quantifies over ∀ (D : Category) and the size discipline is carried by universe polymorphism, which the file header (Structure/Complete.v:27-37) documents explicitly and which is exercised in practice (Adjunction/SAFT.v records that instantiating Complete forces the diagram category's hom universe to match C's). So this is the universe-polymorphic rendering of 'all small limits', not the inconsistent all-diagrams reading.

verifier.notes: Blind pass reached the same. Note also that the in-tree instance is stated for an arbitrary target D (any Cartesian D), which is more general in the target than Awodey's D = Sets, but far weaker in the limit shape. Instance/Fun.v:101-105 records the general pointwise-inheritance principle only as a header comment, explicitly citing nLab — it is not proved.

statement_record.book: A category is cocomplete when it possesses all small colimits — every functor from a small index category into it has a colimit; stated as the formal dual of completeness.
statement_record.intree: Cocomplete {C} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Colimit F, with Colimit F := Limit (F^op) — i.e. cocompleteness IS completeness read in the opposite category, exactly the dual Awodey names.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, with the same universe-polymorphic rendering of smallness as for Complete (the header of Structure/Complete.v documents it). The duality is definitional here, not merely asserted: because the library builds duality into its definitions (C^op^op = C by reflexivity), Colimit/Cocone are literal op-readings of Limit/Cone, and the definition is load-bearing — Theory/Adamek/Corollaries.v:59 `adamek_cocomplete` consumes `@Cocomplete C` to supply the ω-chain colimit. No concrete category is proved cocomplete in-tree, but that is a question about instances, not about the definition this item states.

statement_record.book: Prop 8.10: for any small C and any presheaf P ∈ Sets^(C^op), P is a colimit of representables: with J := the category of elements of P and A : J → C the projection, colim_J (y ∘ A) ≅ P. The proof takes the cocone component at (x,C) to be x : yC → P under the Yoneda correspondence and verifies the universal property.
statement_record.intree: The same content in COEND form. prof_unit_left_iso : prof_compose prof_id P ≅[Fun] P is the natural isomorphism ∫^m C(−,m) × P(m,−) ≅ P in the functor category (specializing at D = 1 this is exactly P ≅ ∫^m P(m) × y(m) for a presheaf); coyoneda_reduction gives the same reduction pointwise in Sets, ∫^x C(x,c) × F x ≅ F c, for F : C ⟶ Sets and each c.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in PRESENTATION and in the missing bridge: the coend ∫^m P m × y m IS the colimit Awodey names, but in-tree there is no proof that a coend is a colimit (Structure/Coend.v defines Coend F := @End (C^op)(D^op)(F^op) and Instance/Sets/Coend.v builds the apex as an inductive setoid quotient by the dinaturality relation; neither is connected to Structure/Limit.v's Colimit class), and there is no category of elements to serve as the index J. On the other side, prof_unit_left_iso is genuinely natural (an iso in [C^op ∏ D, Sets]) and axiom-free, so the naturality Awodey's cocone argument establishes is present in the coend rendering.
